title: observability-log-ingestion-trace-drop-debug-notes-wip
body:
Goal: capture incident breadcrumbs for traces/metrics/log ingestion drop affecting api-gateway and related services. These are personal debug notes - commands tried, observed errors, hypotheses, and next steps.

Symptoms:
- Traces for api-gateway and ingest services dropped ~02:15-03:30 UTC on 2026-02-27 (customer reports + internal dashboards).
- Prometheus metrics (requests_total, latency_histograms) show a sharp drop exactly same window.
- Logs still arriving from most app pods, but log ingestion pipeline reported occasional parse failures and increased consumer lag.
- Alerts: exporter_queue_length for otel-collector > 1200, kafka consumer lag on topic otel-traces peaked at ~1.2M.

Timeline (reconstructed):
- 02:10 UTC: small spike in request latency from edge (ingress).
- 02:15 UTC: metrics and traces start to drop on dashboards.
- 02:16-02:45 UTC: automated retries from sampler + collector increased; queue length grows.
- 02:46 UTC: first alert fired (queue_length).
- 02:50 UTC: attempted restart of otel-collector replica 0 (manual).
- 03:00 UTC: scaled otel-collector replicas from 2 -> 4.
- 03:12 UTC: traces start trickling back; metrics partially recovered by 03:30 UTC.

Commands I ran (copy for reproducibility):
- kubectl -n observability get pods -o wide
- kubectl -n observability logs deployment/otel-collector -c otel-collector --since=4h | tail -n 300
- kubectl -n observability exec -it deploy/otel-collector -- curl -s localhost:8888/metrics | grep exporter_queue_length
- kubectl -n kafka exec -it kafka-0 -- kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group otel-collector-group
- kubectl -n observability exec -it deploy/otel-collector -- /bin/sh -c 'ls /var/lib/collector/queue; du -sh /var/lib/collector/queue/*'
- curl -sS http://api-gateway.internal:9411/health || true
- tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/otel-traffic.pcap port 4317 & (captured a short window)

Key log snippets observed (sanitized):
- 2026-02-27T02:18:12Z otelcol exporter error: exporting traces failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (1234567 vs 1048576)
- 2026-02-27T02:21:05Z kafka consumer error: OffsetOutOfRange for partition 7, resetting to earliest
- 2026-02-27T02:29:44Z prometheus remote write: timeout while sending batch (context deadline exceeded)
- 2026-02-27T02:47:10Z otelcol: queue_length=1420; dropping 120 spans due to backpressure

What these errors mean (initial interpretation):
- The OTLP exporter to our tracing backend was hitting gRPC message size limits ("received message larger than max"). Large traces or batching with default limits can trigger this and cause exporter failures. When exporter fails, collector queue grows -> backpressure -> sampler/processor may drop spans and throttle metrics export.
- Kafka consumer errors (OffsetOutOfRange) are consistent with high producer/consumer churn and possibly retention/compaction edge cases or corrupted offsets caused by prolonged backlog.
- Prometheus remote write timeouts indicate the metrics remote backend was either overloaded or network egress was behaving poorly; remote write blocks can cause drops in scraped series if queue fills up.

Actions tried and immediate results:
1) Restarted otel-collector replica-0 (02:50 UTC) -> short-term reduction in local memory and queue on that pod, but overall queue across replicas still high.
2) Scaled deployment/otel-collector from 2 -> 4 pods (03:00 UTC) -> queue length decreased over 10-15m, traces resumed slowly.
3) Increased exporter gRPC max_message_size in a local dev config and tested with curl -> reproduced "message too large" locally; confirmed size threshold likely culprit.
4) Temporarily tuned exporter to reduce max batch size and enable compression on the exporter (staging test) -> reduced per-message size; no immediate prod config change applied without PR.
5) Investigated Kafka topic (otel-traces): consumer lag high; ran consumer-group reset/checks; decided not to forcibly reset offsets to avoid data loss.
6) Rolled a temporary alert tuning: lowered alert sensitivity for exporter_queue_length -> avoid alert storm while rollback/changes in progress.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- Primary: Collector exporter is sending batches that exceed gRPC max size configured on traces backend (or a gateway load balancer limits gRPC size). This causes exporter failures and queue buildup -> backpressure -> dropped spans and delayed metric writes.
- Secondary: Network egress throttling to the vendor/trace backend caused increased latency/timeouts, compounding queue growth.
- Tertiary: A burst of very large traces (long requests with many spans for a small number of requests) temporarily flooded the exporter; sampling/config limits too permissive for that burst.

Short-term mitigations to apply (candidate list):
- Reduce OTLP exporter batch_size and max_concurrent_requests in the collector config (safe, immediate).
- Enable compression on gRPC exporter (if compatible with backend) to avoid hitting size limits.
- Add a circuit-breaker on exporter failures that returns 429 to upstream sampler to avoid unbounded queue growth.
- Add sampling rule for api-gateway to cap spans per trace for high-cardinality requests.
- Increase replicas of otel-collector during peak windows (automatic scaling) and add HPA based on exporter_queue_length.

Longer-term fixes / follow-ups (create tickets):
- JIRA-4512: "Investigate gRPC message size errors between otel-collector and traces backend - add config change + compatibility test" (linked).
- Confluence note: document recommended OTLP batch size and max message sizes for our backends.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/892 (draft) - reduces default batch size and adds exporter compression flag.
- Add exporter_queue_length > 1000 bump alert and runbook for rapid mitigation (scale/roll collector).

Open questions / unknowns to investigate:
- Exact point where gRPC size limit is enforced: LB, vendor proxy, or backend? Need tcpdump + server-side logs.
- Did any release around 2026-02-27 change default batching behavior? Check infra config PRs between 2026-02-20 and 2026-02-27.
- Why did Prometheus remote write timeout happen at same time - shared egress / network saturation? correlated with trace exporter egress?

Next immediate steps (owned by me):
- [ ] Complete PR to reduce batch defaults and enable compression (draft -> prod) (ETA: today).
- [ ] Add temporary HPA for otel-collector based on exporter_queue_length (small config change, low risk).
- [ ] Run controlled test in staging: replay a large trace to reproduce gRPC message size error and verify compression + batch changes fix it.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to check LB/proxy gRPC size limits and vendor (reach out to Honeycomb/Trace-vendor SRE).

Notes to self / breadcrumbs for followup:
- Saved tcpdump capture to /tmp/otel-traffic.pcap on the node where I ran tcpdump; upload to secure bucket for vendor analysis if needed.
- Do not reset Kafka offsets without archiving current offsets (risky).
- Keep collaborators looped: @Maya for metrics remote write angle, @Ravi for kafka offsets and consumer-group analysis.

If/when this spins up again, immediate handoff checklist for on-call:
- Check exporter_queue_length (prom metric) and kafka consumer lag.
- If queue_length > 1000: scale otel-collector and open ticket; reduce batch size via emergency config change; notify vendor.
- If kafka lag > 500k and consumer errors present: do not reset offsets immediately - escalate to eng-observability.

End of notes. Will update after staging replay results and PR merge.
